title: Throttle Gatekeeper Daybook and Rollback Ladder (May 2027) - notes
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact, day-of ops daybook for the throttled, staged rollout of the routing+quantization change (PR 4123). Primary goal: keep global latency under 240ms p50 while allowing safe gradual capacity expansion; second goal: provide a clear rollback ladder and comms matrix so on-call and release leads can act fast.

Scope:
- Applies to hosted API model routing changes (canary -> staggered regional ramp).
- Includes traffic throttle knobs, telemetry gates, and stepwise rollback procedures.
- Not a full runbook for infra failures (see infra-incident-runbook) but assumes SRE involvement for infra-level escalations.

Assumptions / context (notes to self):
- Canary (region-us-west1) already at 0.5% for 24h, initial perf curves look good.
- PR 4123 changes default batching heuristics and adds quantization profile v2b.
- Dedicated customers pinned to model-v1 are unaffected, routing rule edgedelta-2027 toggles only public pooled routes.
- Budget: tolerate up to 1.5x token cost during initial ramp; abort if cost >2x for >2h.

Preflight checklist (T-48h -> T-2h):
- [ ] Confirm feature-flag default state and canary toggle command (ff: routing/edge-delta).
- [ ] Attach owners to release timeline (lead: Priya; backup: Derek; SRE oncall: Maya).
- [ ] Ensure dashboards ready: latency-by-model, tail-latency burnup, kvcache-hit-rate, burst-surge telemetry.
- [ ] Smoke test script updated and run against staging with quant-profile v2b (script: ci/release/smoke_quant_v2b.sh).
- [ ] Verify autoscaler policies will not aggressively scale down GPU pools during first 2h of ramp (policy: autoscale-lock=2h).
- [ ] Notify growth and CS of potential customer-facing perturbations (Slack ping + #release-notice).
- [ ] Confirm rollback artifacts exist (artifact: rollback-image:runtime:2027-04-29).

Hour-by-hour ramp plan (Day-of):
- 00:00 - 00:30 (canary verification):
  - enable routing/edge-delta for us-west1 at 1% of baseline traffic.
  - watch p50/p95/p99; verify p95 delta < +40ms and p99 < +150ms.
  - sample 10 requests for QA quick-check (QA owner: Owen).
- 00:30 - 02:00 (micro-ramp):
  - increase to 5% if telemetry green (no >2x cost, no >2x tail-latency).
  - run key synthetic prompts from perf-suite and sanity-check outputs (regression tolerance matrix attached).
- 02:00 - 06:00 (regional ramp):
  - if stable, expand to 20% across us-west1 & us-central1.
  - set throttle-gate 1: token-cost alert at 60m window; if triggered, pause ramp and evaluate.
- 06:00 - 18:00 (stability soak):
  - hold at 20% and observe for at least 12h; perform lightweight A/B evals for output quality.
- 18:00 - 24:00 (gradual global expansion):
  - step to 40% then 60% with 2h observation windows.

Telemetry gates (hard and soft):
- Soft gate (monitor-only):
  - p50 increase > 30ms sustained for 10m -> notify release lead (Slack).
  - kvcache-hit-rate drop > 15% -> triage (possible config mismatch).
- Hard gate (auto stop / rollback):
  - p99 > 400ms for 5m -> immediate halt rollback ladder step 1.
  - error-rate increase > 1% absolute (from baseline) for 10m -> immediate halt.
  - cost > 2x historical 1h baseline for 30m -> stop ramp and investigate.

Rollback ladder (fastest safe path):
1) Pause rollout: flip ff routing/edge-delta -> paused (fast toggle). Document who flips and when.
2) Throttle back to previous weight set (manual): set region weights back to 0%/100% baseline via routing service.
3) If partial degradations continue, roll runtime image back to rollback-image:runtime:2027-04-29 using deployment tag mirror.
4) If infra-level errors persist (node oom, gpu failures), escalate to SRE runbook (link in linked_artifacts).

Communications matrix (who says what):
- On-call engineer (Maya): triage and telemetry notes in the watch-channel, call stack if infra issue.
- Release lead (Priya): decision to continue/pause/rollback; updates to #release-notice every milestone.
- Product/CS (Owen): prepare customer statements and coordinate proactive CS messages if rollback occurs.
- Exec/Legal: only if customer-impacting outage >30m or P0 incident.

Run commands cheat-sheet (copy into runbox):
- Toggle FF: curl -X POST https://flags.redwood/api/toggle?flag=routing/edge-delta&state=paused -H 'Auth: $TOKEN'
- Adjust region weights: curl -X PATCH https://routing.redwood/api/set-weights -d '{"us-west1":0.2,"us-central1":0.8}'
- Roll runtime image: ./ops/deploy.sh --image runtime:2027-04-29 --region us-west1
- Quick rollback (emergency): ./ops/fast-rollback.sh --tag 2027-04-29; note: requires SRE approval flag

Release notes draft (skeleton, for release page):
- Title: routing + quantization opt (v2b) rollout - May 2027
- Summary: Reduced per-token latency by ~12% on average for medium-length prompts; introduces quantization profile v2b for CPU-backed fallbacks.
- Impact: gradual rollout, small risk of transient tail-latency increases during warmup. Dedicated customers unaffected unless opted in.
- Known issues: occasional kvcache cold-starts on low-traffic models; observed in staging only so far.
- Migration actions: none required by customers.

Post-deploy checklist (T+0 -> T+72h):
- [ ] Confirm synthetic traffic quality checks pass after each expansion window.
- [ ] Run regression eval set overnight and compare against baseline; file ticket if >1% regression in key prompts.
- [ ] Consolidate release signals into short post (3 bullets) for exec digest.

Open items / TODOs (triage):
- [ ] Add explicit alerting for kvcache new-key churn (linked to INF-2387).
- [ ] Create short runbook for CS on customer queries about latency variance.
- [ ] Validate billing spike detection metric; currently missing short-window smoothing.

Notes / field observations (working log):
- 2027-05-10: Canary smoke looked fine; p99 spikes at minute boundaries correlated with autoscaler downscales. Flagged to infra team.
- 2027-05-12: QA found one mismatch in deterministic outputs for prompt set P-regen-7 (PR 4123 side-effect). Ticket opened: GH-4582.

Appendix: Quick diagnostics checklist when alerted:
- Check region-snapshot: latency, error-rate, cpu/gpu utilization.
- Validate routing config hash matches deployed manifest (config id in service logs).
- Re-run small synthetic set to identify deterministic drift.

End notes: keep this doc lean; copy key snippets into the playbook that the on-call SRE uses. After this rollout completes, we should bake the successful throttle windows into the autoscaler-policy defaults.

Local links / references:
- perf-suite/runbooks/throttle-matrix.csv
- ci/release/smoke_quant_v2b.sh
- confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Throttle+Policies

-- Priya (release lead)
